query: What is Button and what does Button do?
response:
Button is a commerce optimization platform for brands, retailers, publishers, and creators. In plain English, it helps companies turn mobile traffic from affiliate, creator, publisher, ad, and marketing channels into more completed purchases.

Button’s core job is to make the path from “tap/click” to “buy” work better. Its platform uses identity, deep linking, attribution, and machine-learning/AI optimization to send shoppers to the best conversion experience, reduce broken journeys, preserve attribution, and improve revenue from commerce traffic. 
Button

A few practical examples of what Button does:

Area	What Button helps with
Mobile commerce	Routes users from ads, publisher links, or creator content into the right app or mobile web shopping flow
Affiliate / creator marketing	Improves conversion and attribution for traffic coming from partners
Publishers	Helps publishers maximize revenue from commerce links by identifying the best path to purchase
Retailers / brands	Helps recover or improve performance from traffic that might otherwise lose attribution or fail to convert
AI optimization	Uses “Conversion Tuning” to identify broken or suboptimal user experiences and reroute traffic toward better purchase outcomes

Button says its platform is used by major brands to improve mobile marketing and ad performance through identity, deep linking, and machine learning. 
Button
 It has also described itself as an AI-powered commerce optimization platform focused on improving creator and affiliate marketing performance. 
PSG Equity
 In 2024, Button said it surpassed $1 billion in monthly commerce driven through the platform. 
Button

So the simplest summary is: Button helps brands, retailers, publishers, and creators make more money from commerce traffic by optimizing where shoppers land, how attribution is preserved, and which path is most likely to convert.

query: How does Button work for mobile commerce?
response:
Button works in mobile commerce as an optimization and routing layer between traffic sources and the merchant’s best-converting purchase experience.

When someone taps a shopping link from a publisher, creator, affiliate, ad, email, social post, or mobile web page, Button decides the best path for that specific user and context.

How it works

A shopper taps a commerce link
The tap may come from affiliate content, a creator post, CRM, social, display, or a publisher page.

Button evaluates the tap context
Button looks at factors like device, operating system, browser, app availability, traffic source, and whether attribution could break. Button says mobile traffic can vary across hundreds of OS versions, dozens of browsers, thousands of apps, and many countries, so each tap may need different handling. 
PR Newswire

Button routes the shopper to the best purchase path
Instead of sending everyone to the same mobile web page, Button can route users to the merchant app, app store, mobile web, or another optimized landing flow. Its Conversion Tuning technology is designed to detect broken experiences or attribution loss and reroute traffic to a better conversion path. 
Button

It preserves attribution and tracking
Button works alongside affiliate networks such as Awin, Impact, Partnerize, CJ, and Rakuten, while those networks remain the system of record for contracts, commissions, and reporting. Button focuses on mobile routing, app tracking, and app-to-web commerce optimization. 
Acceleration Partners

It improves monetization for publishers and brands
For publishers, Button helps identify the best path to purchase for traffic they send to retailers, without necessarily changing their existing retailer or affiliate-network relationships. 
PR Newswire
 For retailers, the value is higher conversion, more app installs, better app engagement, and recovered revenue from mobile journeys that otherwise break. 
Button

Simple example

A user reads a BuzzFeed-style shopping article on their phone and taps a link to buy sneakers.

Without Button, that link might open in a mobile browser, lose affiliate tracking, fail to open the app, or send the user to a generic page.

With Button, the tap can be routed dynamically: open the retailer’s app if installed, deep-link to the product page, preserve attribution, or use the best web fallback. The goal is to make the mobile purchase journey smoother and more measurable.

Why it matters

Mobile commerce often breaks because app links, browsers, tracking, and affiliate attribution do not behave consistently. Button’s role is to make each tap more valuable by improving routing, conversion, and measurement. Button’s site reports $100B+ in total commerce driven, 14.4B shopping journeys, 22M app installs, and lift metrics such as 38% conversion lift and 42% sales-per-tap lift, based on Button proprietary data and a commissioned Forrester study. 
Button

Yes — Button can be worth it for ecommerce businesses, especially if the business already relies on mobile app traffic, affiliate marketing, creator partnerships, publishers, or retail media. Button positions itself as a commerce optimization platform that helps brands improve mobile shopping journeys, attribution, and conversion from partner-driven traffic. 
Button

The strongest fit is for larger ecommerce brands or retailers with mobile apps. Public descriptions of Button’s customer base emphasize “large ecommerce companies with mobile apps” focused on affiliate and creator marketing, along with publishers and creators. 
PR Newswire
 If a business is small, has limited mobile volume, or is not investing in affiliate/creator channels, Button may be less immediately valuable.

Where Button’s value appears strongest:

Use case	Why it may be worth it
Mobile commerce	Helps route shoppers into better mobile/app experiences
Affiliate marketing	Improves partner-driven conversion and attribution
Creator commerce	Supports creator-led shopping journeys
Publisher partnerships	Helps monetize commerce intent
Retail media	Expands commerce/advertising inventory opportunities

Button also reports significant platform scale, including more than $25B in all-time commerce and $2.9B in app gross merchandise sales in 2025, which suggests it is built for high-volume commerce programs. 
Button

Bottom line: Button is likely worth evaluating if your ecommerce business has meaningful mobile traffic and wants to grow affiliate, creator, publisher, or retail-media revenue. It is probably not the first tool I’d prioritize for a very small ecommerce store that mainly needs basic storefront, email, SEO, or paid social optimization.

query: Does Button help with mobile app conversions?
response:
Yes. Button is specifically positioned to improve mobile app conversions, especially for affiliate, creator, publisher, and commerce-media traffic.

Button’s mobile optimization tools are designed to route mobile shoppers into the highest-converting path, such as opening the brand’s app, sending the user through an install flow, or falling back to mobile web checkout when needed. Its developer docs describe the Button SDK as opening the brand app, install flow, or web checkout depending on the purchase path. 
Button Developers

Evidence from Button and partner case studies points to meaningful conversion lift:

Example	Reported result
Awin + Button	1.3M app installs, 2.7x in-app conversion rate vs. mobile web, 110% higher revenue per tap in app
impact.com + Button	Apps drove 200% the revenue of web journeys
CJ + Button	Better tracking of mobile app conversions and improved mobile affiliate experiences
Button 2025 platform update	175% increase in app installs, 55% increase in app-to-app sales, 40% higher mobile affiliate revenue

So the practical answer is: yes, Button can help with mobile app conversions when a business already has meaningful mobile traffic and an app or app-based checkout journey. It is most relevant when the problem is broken mobile affiliate tracking, users landing on mobile web instead of the app, poor deep linking, missed attribution, or low conversion from social/creator/publisher traffic.

It is probably less useful for a business that does not have an app, has very low mobile volume, or is looking for a general ecommerce storefront rather than a mobile commerce optimization and attribution layer.

query: Does Button improve affiliate link tracking?

Yes. Button appears specifically designed to improve affiliate link tracking for mobile journeys, especially where standard affiliate links can break down across mobile web, apps, deep links, and affiliate-network attribution.

Button says it works with Mobile Measurement Partners to capture transaction data across in-app and mobile web so affiliate commissioning logic can be enforced more accurately. It also positions its technology around identity, deep linking, and mobile marketing performance. 
Button

The practical benefit is that Button can help brands and publishers track more affiliate-driven purchases that happen after a user taps a link on mobile, especially when the ideal path is from a publisher, creator, or affiliate placement into a retailer’s app. Acceleration Partners describes Button’s PostTap as a mobile app tracking solution that integrates with major affiliate networks. 
Acceleration Partners

That said, Button is not just a generic affiliate link shortener or basic tracking pixel. Its strongest fit is for mobile commerce attribution, app deep linking, and post-click journey optimization. For desktop-only affiliate programs or simple web tracking, a traditional affiliate network or tracking platform may be enough.

query: How does Button handle deep linking?
response:
Button handles deep linking by turning affiliate, creator, and publisher traffic into optimized mobile journeys rather than sending every click to the same mobile web page.

In practice, Button’s system can:

Open the brand’s app when appropriate
If the shopper already has the app installed, Button can route the click directly into the app experience instead of mobile web.

Deep link to a relevant destination
The goal is to preserve intent, so a product, offer, or merchant link can land closer to the right in-app or mobile destination rather than forcing the user to search again.

Prompt install when that is likely better
Button says its AI can dynamically choose whether to open the app, prompt an install, or deep link based on the best expected post-click experience. 
Button

Preserve affiliate and creator tracking
Button positions Reach and related products as deep linking plus app-tracking technology for affiliate network traffic, so brands can drive app installs and incremental growth while keeping affiliate/channel data visible. 
Button
+1

Optimize each link individually
Button describes its platform as treating links uniquely to optimize “Yield, Experience, and Signal,” addressing issues like broken user experiences, inconsistent mobile deep linking, and faulty attribution. 
Button

For creators specifically, Button’s PostTap product is described as a cloud-based app deep linking platform that works with Amazon Associates links, using deep linking and route optimization to increase conversion rates for users who already have the Amazon app. 
posttap.com

Bottom line: Button does not treat deep linking as just a technical redirect. It uses deep linking as part of a broader mobile-commerce routing and attribution layer, deciding whether the best path is app open, app install, or mobile web while preserving monetization and tracking.
